'''''Echinopsis chamaecereus''''' is a species of [[cactus]] from northwestern [[Argentina]] and [[Bolivia]]. [[Synonym (taxonomy)|Synonyms]] include '''''Chamaecereus silvestrii'''''.<ref name=POWO_907548-1/> It has been called the '''peanut cactus'''.<ref name=Ande99p67>{{Citation |last=Anderson |first=Miles |year=1999 |title=Cacti and Succulents : Illustrated Encyclopedia |publication-place=Oxford |publisher=Sebastian Kelly |isbn=978-1-84081-253-4 }}, p. 67</ref> This plant should not be confused with ''Echinopsis silvestrii'', a synonym of ''[[Echinopsis albispinosa]]'', a species with a very different appearance.

==Description==
''Echinopsis chamaecereus'' has long stems about {{convert|1|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} across. Orange flowers up to {{convert|4|cm|in|abbr=on}} wide appear in late spring. In cultivation, ''E. chamaecereus'' is hardy to temperatures as low as {{convert|-7|C|F|abbr=on}} if kept dry.<ref name=Ande99p67/>

==Taxonomy==
''Echinopsis chamaecereus'' was first collected and described in 1896 as ''Cereus silvestrii'' by [[Italian Argentines|Italian-Argentinian]] botanist [[Carlo Luigi Spegazzini]] in the mountains between the provinces of [[Tucumán Province|Tucuman]] and [[Salta Province|Salta]], Argentina.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Spegazzini|first=Carlo|title=Cactacearum Plantensium Tentamen|publisher=Juan A. Alsina|year=1905|location=Buenos Aires, Argentina|pages=51}}</ref> However, subsequent expeditions to the area failed to find the species Spegazzini had collected and it is unknown whether the species has gone extinct since the initial collection.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Lambert|first=Jacques G.|title=Cactus d'Argentine|publisher=Concordia-Roeselare|year=1992|pages=32}}</ref> It was transferred to the genus ''Chamaecereus'' as ''Ch. silvestrii'' by Britton and Rose in 1922.<ref name=POWO_907548-1/> When ''Chamaecereus'' was synonymized with ''Echinopsis'', the combination ''Echinopsis silvestrii'' had already been used, so the [[Nomen novum|replacement name]] ''Echinopsis chamaecereus'' was published in 1983.<ref name=IPNI_907548-1>{{IPNI|taxon=''Echinopsis chamaecereus'' |authority=H.Friedrich & Glaetzle|id=907548-1|access-date=2025-11-13|mode=cs1}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
This plant is a recipient of the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/31628/Echinopsis-chamaecereus/Details | title = ''Echinopsis chamaecereus'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 5 June 2020}}</ref>
